body_markdown:
Sometimes I find cars. That’s pretty easy to explain, since I attend between 30 and 50 shows a year—and those figures are conservative. I love shows! But sometimes, cars find me. Today’s featured example of[Flint’s finest](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/buick-city-once-an-automotive-metropolis-finds-new-life/) is a case in point.


I was leaving my office last year—wait, was it actually 2024? Shoot. Time flies. Anyway, it was a cloudy but warm August day, and I was just a few blocks from work when I spotted a sleek yet Broughamy silver sedan from the Age of Aquarius.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


The car was a gorgeous, apparently unmolested Silver Mist 1969 Electra 225 pillared sedan, one of 14,521 built that year. It was spectacular.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


I know that I rather frequently rag on cars that wear non-colors: black, gray, silver, refrigerator white. That said, I make an exception if the interior color is a particularly pleasing, complementary hue, and such was the case with today’s car.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


It featured a simply terrific deep blue interior, a color which harmonized so well with the Silver Mist paint. You don’t usually see a ’60s Electra with no vinyl top, but I like the look. I also love the pairing of a silver exterior with a red interior.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


This is a standard Electra 225. As previously mentioned, it is one of 14,521 built. The base price was $4302 and curb weight was 4236 pounds. It was one of three different Electra 225 models; the other two were the $4323 two-door hardtop and $4432 four-door hardtop.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


As had been the case since its introduction in 1959 (replacing the Roadmaster at that time), the Electra was the top Buick,[notwithstanding the personal-luxury Riviera](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/klockau-classics/1964-buick-riviera-mitchells-masterpiece/) , which had come onto the scene in 1963.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


The Electra 225 came with standard power steering, power brakes, Turbo Hydra-matic automatic transmission, electric clock, carpet extensions on all door panels, and Custom padded seat cushions.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


1969 Buicks, from LeSabre to Wildcat to executive-level Electra, were all new, but still comfortingly familiar. As the brochure encouraged prospective buyers, “Picture yourself approaching your own 1969 Electra 225 for the first time. You’re about to experience your first rush hour trip home in it.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


“You open the door. Rich Cloth and Madrid-Grain Vinyl invite you inside. You relax in luxury. You turn the ignition key and feel the gentle awakening of Electra’s 430 cubic inch powerplant. But you barely feel it. And barely hear it.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


“Welcome to the clean, quiet world of your Electra 225.”


The fond nickname for these cars,[“Deuce and a Quarter,”](https://www.hagerty.com/media/opinion/klockau-classics/the-1968-buick-electra-225-was-flints-finest/) refers not only to the car’s name but also to its impressive length. I must confess, despite the name, these fabulous cars fell just a little short of the mark, measuring 224.8 inches long. Still, impressive!


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


The Electra 225 was a fine car by any measure, but for those who wanted even more sybaritic luxury, there was the Electra 225 Custom.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


It was available in all the Electra 225 body styles, in addition to a convertible coupe. Said convertible was $4643, and 8,294 were built. Convertibles also featured a standard two-way power seat and power windows.


Thomas Klockau


Oh, and did I mention there were *colors* ? Available hues included Copper Mist, Trumpet Gold, Azure Blue, Cameo Cream, Signal Red, Fire Glow Orange (I really want to see a convertible in that color!), Verde Green, and Turquoise Mist.


Thomas Klockau


Under the hood was the 430-cubic-inch V-8. In 1969 form, it produced 360 hp at 5000 rpm and an impressive 475 lb-ft of torque. If you wanted to pull a luxurious, sleek Airstream trailer with one of these, you would have no problem whatsoever.


[Thomas Klockau](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/tklockau/)


To this day, I don’t know whether this car was for sale, owned by a happy, caring steward, or was in for some minor mechanical repair at the repair shop it was parked in front of. But it was sure pretty! Seeing it made my day. Buick, can we *please* get some elegant new sedans sometime soon? I’d buy one, once I got tired of my Cadillac XTS, which I still love!


Thomas Klockau
